newsitem.title: INDIA: India shares end lower,ITC seen down after results.
newsitem.headline: India shares end lower,ITC seen down after results.

text.p: ** (1345 GMT) - Indian stocks end little changed in
lacklustre trade, low volumes
** Bombay shr index slips 10.01 pts at 3,768.30
** Tobacco conglomerate ITC in market focus; announces
1996/97 net profit of 3.42 bln rupees
Traders say profits below market expectations
** HDFC Bank reports 100 pct rise in 1996/97 net profit,
stock ends nearly two pct higher
** National Exchange index down 0.05 pts at 1,050.85, Delhi
index falls 1.10 pts at 779.56
Indian shares finished flat in featureless trade on Tuesday as traders awaited full-year results of tobacco conglomerate ITC which came after the close of market hours.
ITC, one of India's top 10 private companies announced a 1996/97 (April-March) net profit of 3.42 billion rupees against 2.61 billion in 1995/96.
Traders said they had been expecting the profit of up to 4.0 billion rupees due to stronger margins in tobacco.
"The market was absolutely range bound," said Sanjeev Choithani, chief dealer at brokers Pashupati Advani.
"There was some speculative squaring up in ITC, but overall it was a very dull day."
ITC Ltd which is 31.7 percent owned by Britain's B.A.T Industries Plc said the latest results were unaudited.
"The first impression is that ITC profits have been lower than market expectations," said an analyst at a foreign brokerage in Bombay.
Exports from ITC's tobacco division rose 70 percent to 2.56 billion rupees from 1.50 billion in 1995/96, the company said in a statement.
In kerb deals, ITC shares were quoting at 432.0 rupees against the official close of 439.50 rupees at the Bombay exchange. The stock ended Monday at 448.50 rupees.
The company's board has approved capital expenditure/investment plan of 19 billion rupees over next five years, it said without giving details.
Among other stocks, HDFC Bank shares ended 1.25 rupees higher at 60.50 rupees after the firm posted a 100 percent rise in its 1996/97 net profit to 405 million rupees.
-- Anshuman Daga, Bombay equities desk +91-22-265-9000
